disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing the profession fraudulently, beyond its authorized scope, with gross incompetence, gross negligence, or repeated negligence/incompetence
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing the profession fraudulently, beyond its authorized scope, with gross incompetence, with gross negligence on a particular occasion or negligence or incompetence on more than one occasion

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing while ability is impaired by alcohol, drugs, physical disability, or mental disability
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing the profession while the ability to practice is impaired by alcohol, drugs, physical disability, or mental disability

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being habitually drunk or dependent on or habitual user of narcotics, barbiturates, amphetamines, hallucinogens, or similar drugs
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being habitually drunk or being dependent on, or a habitual user of narcotics, barbiturates, amphetamines, hallucinogens, or other drugs having similar effects

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being convicted of a crime under New York, federal, or equivalent out-of-state law
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being convicted of committing an act constituting a crime under: (i) New York State law or, (ii) Federal law or, (iii) The law of another jurisdiction

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having been found guilty of improper professional practice or misconduct by a duly authorized professional disciplinary agency of another state
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Having been found guilty of improper professional practice or professional misconduct by a duly authorized professional disciplinary agency of another state where the conduct upon which the finding was based would, if committed in New York state, constitute professional misconduct

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having been found by the commissioner of health to be in violation of article thirty-three of the public health law
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Having been found by the commissioner of health to be in violation of article thirty-three of the public health law.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having had license to practice medicine revoked, suspended, or surrendered after disciplinary action in another state
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Having his license to practice medicine revoked, suspended or having other disciplinary action taken, or having his application for a license refused, revoked or suspended or having voluntarily or otherwise surrendered his license after a disciplinary action was instituted by a duly authorized professional disciplinary agency of another state

disciplinary_grounds.description: Refusing to provide professional service to a person because of race, creed, color, or national origin
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Refusing to provide professional service to a person because of such person's race, creed, color, or national origin

disciplinary_grounds.description: Permitting, aiding, or abetting an unlicensed person to perform activities requiring a license

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing the profession while the license is suspended, or wilfully failing to register or notify the department of any change of name or mailing address

disciplinary_grounds.description: Committing unprofessional conduct as defined by the board of regents or commissioner
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Committing unprofessional conduct, as defined by the board of regents in its rules or by the commissioner in regulations approved by the board of regents

disciplinary_grounds.description: A violation of section twenty-eight hundred three-d or twenty-eight hundred five-k of the public health law

definition_quote.value: The practice of the profession of medicine is defined as diagnosing, treating, operating or prescribing for any human disease, pain, injury, deformity or physical condition.
definition_quote.quote: The practice of the profession of medicine is defined as diagnosing, treating, operating or prescribing for any human disease, pain, injury, deformity or physical condition.

drug_authority.value: Licensed physicians may prescribe; statute explicitly authorizes prescribing non-patient-specific regimens to nurses (for immunizations, emergency treatment, various tests), and patient-specific or non-patient-specific orders to pharmacists (for immunizations, HIV PEP, insulin, hormonal contraceptives).
drug_authority.quote: A licensed physician may prescribe and order a non-patient specific regimen to a registered professional nurse, pursuant to regulations promulgated by the commissioner

license_status_types.quote: The licensure status of such licensee shall be "inactive" and he or she shall not be authorized to practice the profession

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: A foreign physician must hold a standard certificate from the Educational Council for Foreign Medical Graduates or pass an exam satisfactory to the state board for medicine. Alternatively, a US resident enrolled in a foreign medical school recognized by the WHO may qualify if they complete formal requirements (except internship/social service), attain a satisfactory score on a qualifying examination accepted by an LCME-approved school, complete one academic year of supervised clinical training, complete required post-graduate hospital training, and pass the licensing examination.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: A foreign physician who holds a standard certificate from the educational council for foreign medical graduates or who has passed an examination satisfactory to the state board for medicine and in accordance with the commissioner's regulations

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: There shall be appointed within the department, by the board of regents, a committee on drug and alcohol abuse, which shall advise the board of regents on matters relating to practice by professional licensees with drug or alcohol abuse problems, and which shall administer the provisions of this section.
